detail: Disproves the recorded observation-capability blocker for Linux Qt Quick and narrows the candidate set with build evidence. A Qt Quick application does register on the AT-SPI bus under QT_ACCESSIBILITY and QT_LINUX_ACCESSIBILITY_ALWAYS_ON: a minimal QML window exposes its frame, text field, button and label, and kalk, a real Kirigami application, exposes its whole keypad. The earlier doubt came from reading the desktop once instead of polling it, because the registration is late; a Qt Widgets control read the same way was equally invisible, so the fault was never Qt Quick. marknote is discarded as a candidate: it requires KF 6.21 and Debian trixie ships 6.13. kalk and kclock both build at both revisions. No runtime product behavior changes.
